lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Data: Scaled Graphs and Measurement Line Plots
lessonRef.focus: picture graphs with a scaled key
lessonRef.title: Concept build A: picture graphs with a scaled key

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph uses a scale of 5 per symbol. A bar shows 3 symbols. What does that bar represent?
With a scale of 2 per symbol, "Dogs" has 6 symbols and "Cats" has 4 symbols. How many more dogs than cats?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching adult. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 1 per symbol. The bar for "Blue" is worth 4 symbols. How many does "Blue" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 1 per symbol, "Dogs" has 6 symbols and "Cats" has 3 symbols. How many more does "Dogs" have than "Cats"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Birds" is worth 2 symbols. How many does "Birds" represent?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: On a scaled bar graph with 1 per symbol, "Dogs" has 9 symbols and "Cats" has 1 symbols. How many more does "Dogs" have than "Cats"?
A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 5 per symbol. The bar for "Bananas" is worth 5 symbols. How many does "Bananas" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 2 per symbol, "Apples" has 6 symbols and "Bananas" has 1 symbols. How many more does "Apples" have than "Bananas"?

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A scaled bar graph shows a survey where each bar length equals a count of 1 per symbol. The bar for "Apples" is worth 1 symbols. How many does "Apples" represent?
On a scaled bar graph with 2 per symbol, "Dogs" has 9 symbols and "Cats" has 6 symbols. How many more does "Dogs" have than "Cats"?
